class.name: MovementInput
class.brief_description: What the player asked for on one simulation tick.
class.description: An object rather than a set of arguments because it is the half of the simulation that has to travel: a predicted client sends this and nothing else, and the server replays it. Everything needed to reproduce a tick is here.

method.name: duplicate_input
method.description: An independent copy of this input. What a prediction history keeps for every tick it may have to replay.

method.name: get_facing_direction
method.description: The requested heading as a horizontal unit vector, or [code]Vector3.ZERO[/code] when there is none. See [member facing_index].

method.name: has_custom_flag
method.description: Whether any bit of [param flag] is set in [member custom_flags].

method.name: has_facing
method.description: Whether this tick asks for a heading - [member facing_index] is not [code]-1[/code].

method.name: set_facing_direction
method.description: Sets [member facing_index] from a direction, rounded to the nearest of [constant FACING_STEPS] headings around world up. A direction with no horizontal part clears the request.

members.member: Sixteen bits a game gives its own meaning - a dash, a sprint, a mantle. They travel with the input, so an action carried in them happens on the same tick on the client that predicts it, on the server and on every replay. Set them with [method CharacterMovementComponent.add_custom_input_flags] and act on them from [signal CharacterMovementComponent.custom_input_flags]. Bits above the sixteenth are dropped.

Which way the character wants to face on this tick: a heading around world up, in steps of [code]TAU / FACING_STEPS[/code] (0 faces +Z), or [code]-1[/code] for no request. Kept as the step rather than a vector so the predicting client and the server turn from bit-identical numbers - the wire carries only the step. Set it through [method CharacterMovementComponent.set_facing_input].

The tick this input belongs to, on the clock of the machine that gathered it. A predicting client numbers its moves with it, and the server answers with the last one it simulated - which is the whole basis of reconciliation.

World space direction, length clamped to 1. The clamp matters: the [Pawn] accumulates input on the render frame and the simulation consumes it on the physics frame, so at 144Hz render and 60Hz physics the vector has been added twice and is twice as long. Left alone, walking speed would rise with the frame rate.

Whether the character wants to be crouched on this tick - a held state, not an event. [method CharacterMovementComponent.crouch] and [method CharacterMovementComponent.un_crouch] set the latch this is read from, and it travels with the input, so a replayed or received move crouches by itself.
Whether a jump was asked for this tick.

constants.constant: How many headings [member facing_index] tells apart - twelve bits on the wire, under a tenth of a degree each.
